<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_profile.py; refreshed nightly by .github/workflows/refresh-profile.yml.
     Keep the alt text on ONE line: a blank line inside a raw HTML block ends the block, which drops
     the <img> and leaves a <picture> that renders nothing at all.
     No width="100%" on the img. A percentage width stretches the panel to whatever the column is,
     which upscaled it 1.22x and read as zoomed. Bare intrinsic width renders 1:1 and can only ever
     shrink, via GitHub's own max-width:100%.
     Width switching ONLY. There is no prefers-color-scheme source here and there must not be one:
     GitHub wraps any theme-aware <picture> in its own themed-picture element, which resolves the
     color-scheme half of a combined query and ignores the width half, so a dark-theme reader got
     the 460px phone panel on a full-width desktop. One dark panel now serves both GitHub themes.
     The breakpoint is 720px because the desktop panel is drawn 960px wide: a column narrower than
     that scales it down, and by ~700px the text is under 11px. Below the breakpoint the 460px
     narrow variant renders at its own size instead, which is legible. -->
<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 720px)" srcset="assets/profile-narrow.svg">
  <img src="assets/profile.svg" alt="Terminal session. whoami: Dylan Fodor, Full-Stack Developer at Software Consulting Services. cat about.txt: I build and modernize the software newspapers use to sell and produce advertising. I lean front-end but work the whole stack, and the work I'm proudest of is the load-bearing kind: two-factor auth, payment processing, and a generative-AI tool that makes print-ready ad artwork. Reliability first, because that's the part people only notice when it's missing. ls -l ~/tools: argus, a call/impact graph over a million-line legacy codebase with cited file:line receipts; aegis, a build-trust engine that compiles on the real host and cannot report a false green; iris, headless visual verification over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, returning a screenshot, a verdict, and console errors; demeter, a dev-database harness that stands up, seeds, and tears down a stack on demand; ariadne, a long-effort tracker that reports the drift between its own claims and what git did; delphi, a personal knowledge engine, a linked note graph with scored recall across sessions; momus, an adversarial reviewer that assumes my change is broken and tries to prove it. tail shipped.log: multi-method two-factor auth on 90+ newspaper sites; a provider-agnostic payment layer and a live processor migration; print-ready ad artwork from a text prompt, three image models behind one interface; Google Ad Manager line items, advertisers, and creatives straight from order entry; a multi-tenant classified-ads marketplace built solo, ad builder to checkout. tail activity.log: recent merged-PR counts, a 30-day trend, and the latest public push, refreshed nightly. cat stack.txt: JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, PHP, SQL; React and Next.js; Node.js, Flask, Express, REST and JSON-RPC APIs; PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis; AWS, Docker, CI/CD, Linux; LLM integration, image generation, speech to text.">
